Watts made this hymn from Psalm 117, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Praise the LORD, all you nations! Extol Him, all you peoples! 2For great is His loving devotion toward us, and the faithfulness of the LORD endures forever. Hallelujah! PSALM 117 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 117
From all that dwell below the skies, Let the Creator's praise arise! Let the Redeemer's name be sung Thro' every land, by every tongue. STANZA I
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 2. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.

Printed hymnals list, for each hymn, the Bible passages it goes with, so a church can choose a hymn for the day's reading. Gathered from the hymnals Hymnary.org catalogues, editors have tied this hymn to 21 passages in 7 books. One square is one passage; a ringed square is one the hymn's own lines echo.
